findings.comment: Building elevations with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions are not provided. Plan view only shows OHE line locations without vertical clearance data needed to verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductors to building faces.
applicableAreas: buildings near overhead electric lines on southern and eastern boundaries

findings.comment: Site plan shows overhead electric conductors (OHE) running along western and southern boundaries near proposed buildings, but no clearance dimensions from the outer conductor to any building face are provided. No horizontal sky-to-ground clearance dimensions are documented on plan or elevation sheets. Add dimension annotations on site plan and building elevation sheets showing minimum 7.5-foot horizontal clearance from outside conductor to all building edges.
applicableAreas: Buildings 1-8 and adjacent overhead electric conductors on western and southern site boundaries

findings.comment: Overhead electric line shown on site plan running along southern property boundary, but no surveyed conductor elevation data or clearance dimensions provided. Building elevations sheets not included in site plan set, preventing verification of 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement.
applicableAreas: Buildings 6, 7, 8 south elevation relative to overhead electric line

findings.comment: The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies to all customer facilities. No profile, section, or elevation views are provided showing radial clearance measurements from outside conductors to building footprints, parking areas, or other site features in three dimensions.
applicableAreas: customer facilities near overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors on southern and eastern boundaries

findings.comment: Overhead electric lines (OHE) are shown on plans but are not labeled with voltage classification. The 15-foot radial clearance requirement applies only to distribution facilities operating below 60kV (typically 12.47kV or 34.5kV in Austin). Without voltage labeling, the applicability of this distribution-specific requirement cannot be determined. Verify whether shown OHE lines are distribution or transmission facilities and label with operating voltage on utility plans.
applicableAreas: Buildings and facilities proximate to overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Overhead distribution line present on site plan, but no clearance dimensions or radial clearance verification provided. No horizontal plan details showing 15-foot radial clearance from outside conductor to any customer facilities or site features.
applicableAreas: Building locations relative to overhead distribution line at southern boundary

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the 39-sheet site plan set. Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and dimensioned clearances are required to demonstrate compliance with clearance requirements when buildings are within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities.
applicableAreas: all buildings and elevated structures near overhead facilities

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the site plan package showing surveyed overhead conductor elevations and locations. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations but provides no conductor elevation data. Building elevation sheets with registered surveyor data showing conductor heights and clearance dimensions to building faces and projections are required to verify vertical clearance compliance. Provide building elevations with surveyed conductor elevation callouts.
applicableAreas: All buildings within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in this site plan set. Surveyed elevations and locations of overhead conductors required to demonstrate clearances are not provided on any available document.
applicableAreas: Buildings 6, 7, 8 relative to southern overhead electric line

findings.comment: No section or profile views are provided showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edge of buildings and building projections. Site plan shows buildings near overhead lines but lacks dimensioned clearance verification exhibits required by code.
applicableAreas: all buildings and building projections within potential clearance distance of overhead facilities

findings.comment: Section and profile views with dimension callouts from the outside conductor to building edges are absent from the site plan. Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) references 'See Sht. 19 for Profile' but Sheet 19 is a water/wastewater utility tap plan, not electrical clearance profiles. No dimension lines originating at conductor locations and extending to outermost building edges are provided on any sheet. Provide section/profile exhibits with specific clearance dimensions from outside conductor to all building faces and projections.
applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and building projections within clearance distance of overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: Section and profile views showing dimensions from the outer electric conductor to outermost building edges are not provided on the site plan. While a site plan drawing exists, it contains only plan-view (top-down) information with no vertical section views depicting conductor-to-building clearances.
applicableAreas: All buildings and building projections near overhead electric line

findings.comment: Driveways and parking areas are proposed throughout the site. Grading plan shows finished floor elevations for buildings and finished grade in parking areas. However, no surveyed mid-span clearance measurements are provided showing the lowest point of overhead lines (including any attached equipment) relative to driveway and parking surface elevations. Determination of whether truck traffic will use driveways to establish 16-foot vs. 18-foot requirement is not explicitly documented.
applicableAreas: driveways and parking areas throughout site

findings.comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) and site plan (Sheet 9) show driveway alignments and elevations, but no cross-section views document vertical clearance from finished driveway surface to lowest point of overhead electric conductors (including telecommunications attachments). The 16-foot minimum clearance (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot clearance (areas with truck traffic) must be verified through section views with dimension callouts. Provide section views showing driveway finished grade elevation and overhead line clearance dimensions; verify whether truck traffic is expected.
applicableAreas: Proposed driveways near overhead electric lines where vertical clearance applies

findings.comment: While the grading plan (Sheet 11) shows driveway locations and elevations, no section views showing vertical clearances from the overhead electric line to the driveway surface are provided. Mid-span clearance verification required by code is not documented.
applicableAreas: Driveways throughout site relative to overhead electric line

findings.comment: No clearance dimensions are provided on any site plan sheets showing measurements from the outside conductor (outermost electric line) to buildings, structures, walls, or other site features. Where clearance dimensions should be shown (such as on building elevation sheets or section views), none are present. The measurement standard (from outside conductor, not from pole centerline) cannot be verified because no dimensions are shown.
applicableAreas: all clearance dimensions on site plan

findings.comment: Critical requirement: all clearance dimensions must be measured from the OUTSIDE CONDUCTOR, never from utility pole centerline. Multi-conductor installations have conductors offset several feet from pole center. Currently, no clearance dimensions are shown on any plan sheets, so this measurement methodology cannot be verified. When clearance dimensions are provided, ensure dimension lines originate at the conductor location (not pole center) and extend to the outermost edge of the site feature being cleared.
applicableAreas: Any clearance dimensions shown on site plan sheets

findings.comment: Site plan shows distance dimensions from buildings to property boundary (29.6', 45.9', 21.3'), but these are NOT clearance dimensions from the overhead electric conductor. Code requires clearance dimensions measured from the outside conductor, not from the property boundary or utility pole centerline. The overhead conductor location is not dimensioned relative to these distance measurements.
applicableAreas: Clearance dimensions shown on site plan

findings.comment: Electric easements (5-foot electric easements and 7.5-foot PUE per plat dedication) are shown on site plan. Overhead distribution facilities exist within and adjacent to these easement areas. Site features (buildings, walls, parking) are shown in proximity to these easements, but clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to items within the easement are not provided. The absolute prohibition against facilities under or over distribution lines, as distinct from the 7.5-foot clearance requirement, cannot be verified without elevation data showing vertical spatial relationships.
applicableAreas: all buildings and site features within electric easements on southern and eastern boundaries

findings.comment: UCM § 1.10.3 contains an absolute prohibition: customer facilities shall NOT be installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities, distinct from the clearance distance requirements and independent of measured clearance. Existing survey shows OHE lines; site plan shows buildings and structures in proximity. Plans must affirmatively demonstrate that no buildings, building projections, overhangs, or other permanent structures are positioned directly beneath or above the overhead distribution conductor routing. Any facility within electric easement must maintain 7.5-foot clearance. Provide clearance verification on all plan sheets showing OHE routing relative to structures.
applicableAreas: All buildings, structures, and site features relative to overhead distribution electric lines shown on site boundary

findings.comment: Site plan shows electric easements (5-foot electric easements from Mecey Subdivision plat recorded as C8S-75-160) but provides no documentation of compliance with the prohibition on installing customer facilities under or over overhead distribution facilities. Code requires absolute prohibition of structures within electric easements (separate from clearance distance requirements). No clearance verification or facility-exclusion documentation provided.
applicableAreas: Structures or site features within electric easement areas

findings.comment: Driveway and parking area elevations are shown on the grading plan. Overhead electric facilities exist on the site. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is provided showing the vertical distance from the lowest point of overhead conductors (including any attached equipment like transformers) to proposed driveway and parking surface elevations. When vertical clearance appears marginal based on available data, surveyor-certified field measurements of mid-span clearances are required.
applicableAreas: driveways and parking areas throughout site

findings.comment: Vertical clearances from overhead electric lines to buildings, driveways, and parking areas appear potentially marginal based on site elevations and estimated overhead line heights shown on existing survey. No registered surveyor mid-span clearance survey data is provided. When overhead lines cross or are adjacent to site features with height constraints (driveways requiring 16-18 feet, buildings requiring clearance), a registered professional surveyor must provide measured pole and conductor elevation data showing actual mid-span clearances. Hire registered surveyor to conduct mid-span clearance survey showing actual conductor elevations and clearances to all site features.
applicableAreas: All locations where overhead electric lines are adjacent to proposed buildings, driveways, parking, or other structures with vertical clearance concerns

findings.comment: Vertical clearance from overhead electric line to proposed driveways appears potentially marginal based on available site elevation data. Registered surveyor survey of pole locations and mid-span clearances is not provided to verify minimum vertical clearance requirements (16-foot or 18-foot) are met.
applicableAreas: Driveways and features at southern property boundary

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows 3 mitigation trees (marked 'M') positioned within 10 lateral feet of the overhead electric line (-OHE-) on the southern property boundary. UCM § 1.10.10.4 requires trees within 50 lateral feet of transmission lines (or 10 lateral feet of distribution lines) to be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked UC with mature height generally ≤20 feet). The plant list (Sheet 35) identifies proposed shade trees as Live Oak and Cedar Elm, and ornamental trees as Texas Mountain Laurel and Mexican Redbud, but does not explicitly verify that any of these species are marked utility-compatible or that the specific 3 mitigation trees near the overhead line are one of these approved species. No species identification is provided for the 3 mitigation trees shown on the landscape plan near the overhead lines.
applicableAreas: 3 mitigation trees on southern property boundary within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows trees in proximity to overhead electric line (OHE) running along southern and eastern boundaries, identified only by classification codes (M, SY, PL) without species identification. No lateral distances from trees to conductors are documented. Trees within 10 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors (or 50 lateral feet of transmission conductors) must be from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked 'UC', generally mature height ≤20 feet). Provide tree species identification on landscape plan by reference to plant schedule (Sheet 32 or detailed plant list), verify species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible list, and document lateral distances from trees to OHE. Relocate any non-compatible trees outside the clearance zones.
applicableAreas: Tree planting locations on landscape plan near overhead electric distribution and transmission conductors

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows proposed trees (Mitigation Trees marked 'M' and Parking Lot Trees marked 'PL') located within 10-50 feet lateral distance from the existing overhead electric distribution line at the southern property boundary. No documentation provided verifying that these proposed tree species (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel) are included in ECM Appendix F 'Utility Compatible Shade Trees' list marked 'UC'. Plant list does not reference ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designation for any species.
applicableAreas: Proposed trees within 10-50 lateral feet of overhead distribution line

findings.comment: Down guy wires from distribution poles may exist on the site but are not clearly depicted on the survey or site plan. The existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) includes a legend item for 'guy wires' but the plan view does not explicitly show down guy wire locations or their relationship to proposed accessible paths and driveways. Without explicit down guy location mapping, potential conflicts cannot be definitively identified or resolved. Electric utility infrastructure, including guy wire systems, is frequently omitted from site plans per the grouping's common violation patterns.
applicableAreas: pedestrian pathways and driveways throughout site

findings.comment: Existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols (support cables from poles to ground anchors), indicating down guy presence. However, site plan does not address whether down guys are in conflict with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features, or whether they have been relocated or poles converted to self-supporting structures. Down guy wires and anchor locations must be verified against all proposed site features and either relocated or resolved through pole conversion. Provide down guy relocation notes or conversion specifications for any poles with down guys that conflict with site improvements.
applicableAreas: Down guy wire anchor locations shown on existing survey conflicting with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or other site features

findings.comment: Down guy wires from existing electric distribution poles are not explicitly depicted on the site plan, though the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations along the southern boundary. The legend indicates poles (UTILITY POLE symbol) but down guy wire anchor locations are not detailed. If down guy wires exist from the overhead distribution line, they may conflict with proposed driveways or accessible routes. Guy wire locations and resolutions (relocation vs. pole conversion) are not documented.
applicableAreas: Existing down guy wires from poles on or near property

findings.comment: Down guy anchor locations (if they exist) are not explicitly mapped on the site plan or easement exhibits. The survey legend includes guy wire symbols but these are not clearly identified on the survey drawing. Without explicit down guy anchor point locations with associated 10-foot-wide and 5-foot-extension easement boundaries shown on an easement exhibit, compliance with this documentation requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: if down guy anchors from distribution poles exist on site

findings.comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles with guy wire symbols indicating down guy anchors. Site plan and easement exhibit must show dedicated down guy anchor easements (10-foot wide extending minimum 5 feet past ground entry point of anchor) for each down guy anchor visible on survey. If down guys are relocated or removed, provide relocation notes. Provide down guy anchor easement exhibits showing 10-foot width and minimum 5-foot extension from each visible down guy anchor on existing survey.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor points from distribution poles on site

findings.comment: Down guy anchor points from distribution poles are not detailed on the existing conditions survey or site plan. If down guy anchors exist supporting the existing overhead distribution line, dedicated easements (10-foot width extending 5 feet past anchor ground entry) are not identified. Applicant must coordinate with Austin Energy to identify existing guy anchor locations and verify easement designations.
applicableAreas: Existing down guy anchor points from distribution poles

findings.comment: No construction logistics plan, site logistics plan, or construction phasing plan is included in the submitted site plan set that maps construction staging areas, equipment laydown zones, crane swing radius, or work platforms. Without these plans showing staging area boundaries with 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead lines maintained during construction, the working clearance requirement (OSHA 1910.333, UCM § 1.10.2) cannot be verified to be satisfied.
applicableAreas: construction staging areas, equipment laydown, crane operations

findings.comment: During construction, staging areas, crane swing radii, material storage, scaffold locations, and equipment operation zones must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from energized overhead electric lines per OSHA 1910.333. This is a working clearance requirement distinct from permanent clearances. No construction phasing plan or logistics plan has been provided in the site plan package showing staging area boundaries and confirming 10-foot working clearance during all construction phases. Provide construction logistics plan or phasing plan showing staging areas and confirming 10-foot radial clearance from OHE during all construction phases.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas, equipment operation zones, and work platforms during site construction

findings.comment: No site logistics plan or construction staging plan is provided with this site plan set. During construction, equipment operation zones, work platforms, and staging areas must maintain 10-foot radial clearance from overhead electric lines per OSHA/UCM § 1.10.2. This requirement applies during construction and is separate from permanent clearances. Contractor must maintain required clearances during construction near the overhead line at southern boundary.
applicableAreas: Construction staging areas and equipment zones during construction

findings.comment: The required note stating 'Owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines' per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 is not included on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. This notification requirement is mandatory when overhead electric lines exist on or adjacent to a site with construction activities. The absence of this critical safety note from the plan set is non-compliant.
applicableAreas: entire site, all construction activities

findings.comment: Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003 requires plans to include a note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines. This note is not present on the cover sheet or general notes sheets. Review of Sheets 1 and 3 found no such notification requirement. Add a general note on cover sheet stating: 'Owner/Contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before commencement of any work near high-voltage overhead electric lines per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.'
applicableAreas: Cover sheet or general notes for project with overhead electric lines and construction activities

findings.comment: Sheet 3 contains a 48-hour notification requirement in the Electric Transmission Notes (Item 3), but the note is titled 'Electric Transmission Notes' and specifically references transmission facilities. The note states: 'A pre-construction safety meeting is required with Austin Energy 48 hours before commencement of construction.' However, this note is limited to transmission facilities and does not apply to the distribution line shown on the site plan. Code requires 48-hour notification before work near high-voltage overhead lines (including both transmission and distribution). No general notification requirement for the overhead distribution line is provided on the cover sheet or general notes.
applicableAreas: General site construction near overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Mitigation trees proposed near the overhead electric distribution line are not identified by species on the landscape plan. Species identification is required to verify utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F. Identify tree species for all trees within 25 feet of the overhead distribution conductor and cross-reference to ECM Appendix F to verify utility-compatible designation.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary near overhead electric line (OHE)

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows mitigation trees (marked 'M') near the overhead electric distribution line (OHE) on south edge, but plant schedule does not indicate which specific tree species are located at each 'M' position. Utility-compatible status of proposed trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud) cannot be verified without cross-referencing species against ECM Appendix F utility-compatible designations and confirming specific species placement locations on landscape plan.
applicableAreas: Area south of site along overhead electric distribution conductor

findings.comment: Overhead distribution conductors are shown on the landscape plan and existing conditions survey running along the site boundaries. Proposed mitigation trees (marked 'M' symbol) are shown directly adjacent to the OHE line on the bottom property boundary. However, the species of these mitigation trees cannot be determined from the landscape plan because the plant legend does not identify species—it only provides functional categories (M = Mitigation Tree). The plant schedule on Sheet 35 identifies species using a different symbol system (geometric circles) that does not correspond to the symbols used on the landscape plan. Additionally, no explicit lateral distances are dimensioned from the proposed tree trunks to the conductors, making it impossible to verify that non-utility-compatible trees are not within the 15-foot minimum clearance for distribution facilities.
applicableAreas: Property boundary along Valley View Road (western boundary), bottom property boundary (southern boundary)

findings.comment: Utility pole locations are not identified on the landscape plan. Without specific pole locations plotted, the distance from proposed trees to poles cannot be verified. Show utility pole locations and add dimension lines demonstrating minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from tree trunk center to pole.
applicableAreas: southern property boundary along OHE

findings.comment: Utility pole locations are not depicted on the landscape plan. The plan's key notes do not include a pole symbol, and no poles are explicitly labeled or shown. Without pole locations on the landscape plan, proximity of trees to poles cannot be verified. This is particularly critical because poles may be located off-site (on adjacent public right-of-way) but still require the 10-foot clearance per UCM § 1.10.10.4.
applicableAreas: Locations where overhead electric poles may be present

findings.comment: Utility poles are shown on the existing conditions survey (Sheet 4) along the property boundaries with overhead electric lines. Proposed mitigation trees (marked 'M') are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) directly adjacent to the OHE line at the property boundary. However, no explicit lateral distances are dimensioned from the tree trunks to the utility poles. The visual proximity suggests trees may be within the 10-foot minimum clearance, but without explicit dimensioned distances, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Property boundary along Valley View Road (western boundary), bottom property boundary (southern boundary)

findings.comment: The landscape plan legend identifies trees only by functional category (SY, PL, P, M), not by species. Species names must be added to the landscape plan legend or directly adjacent to tree symbols to allow reviewers to verify utility compatibility per ECM Appendix F. Update landscape plan to show species names for all trees, particularly those proposed within 25 feet of overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: landscape plan, all tree locations, particularly trees near overhead electric facilities

findings.comment: The landscape plan designates trees near the overhead electric line with a generic 'M' (mitigation tree) symbol. The plant schedule on Sheet 35 provides overall tree species and quantities but does not cross-reference which specific species are placed at each 'M' location on the landscape plan. Trees proposed near overhead electric facilities must be identified by species on or near the landscape plan to allow verification of utility-compatibility and clearance compliance. The current documentation requires cross-referencing two separate sheets to determine species identification, which does not constitute adequate plan notation per standard reviewer practice.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan Sheet 31 and plant schedule Sheet 35

findings.comment: The plant legend on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) identifies trees only by functional category (M = Mitigation Tree, SY = Street Yard Tree, PL = Parking Lot Tree, P = Parking Buffer Point Tree) without identifying species. While a plant schedule with species names is provided on Sheet 35, that schedule uses a different symbol system (geometric symbols: circle with cross, circle with hash, circle with wavy edge, circle with jagged edge) that does not match the letter symbols used on the landscape plan. Therefore, a reviewer examining the landscape plan cannot determine the species of the proposed mitigation trees near electric facilities. Provide a cross-reference between the landscape plan symbols and the plant schedule species, or add species identification directly to the landscape plan legend.
applicableAreas: Property boundary—proposed mitigation trees adjacent to overhead electric line (southern property boundary)

findings.comment: Cannot verify whether proposed trees are within prohibited clearance zones due to lack of species identification and distance measurements. If trees proposed within restricted zones (per species/height/distance analysis) are approved, provide documented written approval from Austin Energy authorizing the exception.
applicableAreas: mitigation trees near overhead electric line

findings.comment: No documented written approval from Austin Energy is provided in the submitted plans authorizing any trees to be planted within the restricted clearance zones established by UCM § 1.10.10.4. This item is conditionally applicable: if trees are determined to violate clearance restrictions (per evaluations of EL-2.1, EL-2.3, EL-2.6, EL-2.7, EL-2.8), then explicit Austin Energy approval would be required. Since the tree species and exact placement cannot be verified (per EL-2.1 and EL-2.10 findings), and clearances are not dimensioned (per EL-2.12/EL-2.13), it cannot be determined whether trees are actually within prohibited zones. Therefore, applicability of this approval requirement cannot be established.
applicableAreas: Trees proposed near overhead electric distribution conductor and equipment

findings.comment: Proposed mitigation trees are shown directly adjacent to the overhead distribution line at the property boundary, suggesting potential proximity to prohibited clearance zones (less than 15 feet for non-utility-compatible trees, less than 25 feet for large trees, less than 10 feet for poles). However, because (1) the species of these trees cannot be determined from the landscape plan, and (2) no explicit distances are dimensioned, it cannot be verified whether the trees are actually within prohibited zones. Additionally, no documented written approval from Austin Energy is visible in the submitted plans. If the proposed trees are determined to be within prohibited clearance zones, explicit written approval from Austin Energy would be required. This approval is not provided.
applicableAreas: Property boundary—proposed mitigation trees adjacent to overhead electric line (southern property boundary)

findings.comment: Transformer Pads 2 and 3 are located immediately adjacent to building walls with visual clearance estimated at only 2-5 feet, falling significantly short of the required 5-foot minimum clearance from brick/masonry buildings per UCM § 1.10.4 Table 1.10.4. No dimensions are marked on the electrical plan to verify clearance compliance.
applicableAreas: Pad 2 (west of Building 2, Unit 201)
Pad 3 (west of Building 8, Unit 801)

findings.comment: Specific horizontal clearance dimensions from transformer pads to buildings, structures, and building foundations are not shown or dimensioned on the electrical design plan. While five transformer pads are clearly labeled and located, no measurements indicating compliance with minimum 5-foot clearance requirements are provided.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations

findings.comment: Transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan, but specific clearance dimensions from buildings are not labeled. Visual scale analysis suggests some pads may not meet the 5-foot minimum clearance from adjacent buildings, but definitive verification cannot be made without explicit dimension callouts.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: No fences or gates are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) adjacent to transformer pads. The site plan (Sheet 9) does not show fences at transformer pad locations. Without fences shown on the plans, this requirement is not applicable. However, if fences are proposed in the landscape or site plan, the clearance requirements (5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3 feet for sides without) must be verified.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

findings.comment: Site plan shows various features but no fences or gates are clearly identified as directly adjacent to transformer pad locations. Fence locations and transformer access door orientations are not sufficiently documented to evaluate clearances.
applicableAreas: Areas adjacent to transformer pads with fences

findings.comment: Site plan shows fences and barriers on the property but transformer pads are shown without access door orientation or clearance documentation from fences. Visual analysis suggests some pads are within fenced areas but specific clearances are not dimensioned.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The electrical plan shows Pads 2 and 3 with approximately 2-5 feet clearance to buildings, which would trigger the reduced clearance exception if the applicant intends to claim it. However, there is no documentation of (1) Austin Energy Design written approval, (2) verification that location is not in confined space, (3) adequate clearance to windows/doors/ducts (10 ft+ requirement), (4) adequate vertical clearance to windows/doors (15 ft+ requirement), or (5) 3-hour fire rating for the clearance area. Without architectural specifications showing fire ratings or AE Design approval letter, compliance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Pad 2 and Pad 3 (if reduced clearances are proposed)

findings.comment: Plans do not clearly show whether clearances less than 5 feet to buildings are proposed. No architectural specifications or fire rating documentation is provided to support any reduced clearance approvals.
applicableAreas: Transformer pad clearance areas

findings.comment: Plans do not show clearance dimensions between transformer pads and buildings. If any pads are located less than 5 feet from buildings, required AE Design written approval documentation and fire rating verification are not provided in the submittal.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: No balconies or building overhangs are visible on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) or site plan (Sheet 9) located directly above or immediately adjacent to any of the five transformer pads. The requirement applies only 'when balconies or overhangs are present above or adjacent to transformer.' Building elevations would be needed to confirm whether overhangs extend over pad locations. This cannot be verified from the current plan set.
applicableAreas: Not determinable from current plan set

findings.comment: Building elevations showing balconies and overhangs relative to transformer pad locations were not reviewed. Vertical clearance documentation above transformer pads is not provided.
applicableAreas: Buildings with balconies or overhangs above transformer locations

findings.comment: Building elevations and cross-sections do not show balconies or overhangs directly above or adjacent to transformer pads, but no cross-section drawings are provided to verify vertical clearances or absence of coverings above pads.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not identify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type, which triggers different clearance requirements. Building elevations showing window/door locations and their heights are not provided in the plan set. Without (1) equipment type specification, (2) building elevation drawings, and (3) measured distances from pads to windows/doors, the 12-foot clearance requirement for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

findings.comment: Building elevations and windows/door locations relative to transformer pads were not examined. This requirement applies to oil-filled equipment but transformer type specifications are not provided on the electrical plan.
applicableAreas: Building facades with windows, doors, or ventilating ducts

findings.comment: No information regarding window or door locations relative to transformer pads is provided. Plans do not identify if transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Required 12-foot horizontal clearance cannot be verified without building elevation documentation and equipment specifications.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The site plan (Sheet 9) shows concrete sidewalks as part of the site infrastructure, but no sidewalks are explicitly shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) positioned adjacent to transformer pads. The location of site sidewalks relative to each transformer pad cannot be clearly determined from the available plans. Dimensions from pads to nearby sidewalk back-of-curb lines are not marked.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads

findings.comment: Site plan indicates sidewalks throughout the development, but specific dimensions from transformer pad edges to sidewalk back-of-curb are not shown or dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Sidewalk locations adjacent to transformer pads

findings.comment: Sidewalks are shown adjacent to some transformer pads on the site plan, but specific dimension callouts showing 2-foot minimum clearance from back of sidewalk are not provided.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not specify whether transformer equipment is oil-filled or dry-type, and no fire escape locations are identified on the plans. The site plan (Sheet 9) does not show fire escapes or stairs serving as fire escapes. Building elevations are not provided. Without equipment type specification and without identification of fire escape locations, the 20-foot horizontal/radial clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if oil-filled)

findings.comment: Building elevations showing fire escape or external stairwell locations were not reviewed. Transformer type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified on the electrical plan.
applicableAreas: Fire escapes and external stairwells

findings.comment: Fire escapes or stairs serving as fire escapes are not explicitly shown on the site plan. No documentation confirms whether equipment is oil-filled or dry-type. Required 20-foot horizontal/radial clearance for oil-filled equipment cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not mark or specify access door orientation for any of the five transformer pads, making it impossible to verify that hot-stick use areas have minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent buildings. This is a required documentation element—transformer pad symbols must indicate which side is the access door, and clearance zones must be dimensioned or clearly marked.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pads

findings.comment: Transformer pad locations are shown on the electrical plan, but specific clearance dimensions from the access door side to adjacent buildings or open areas are not provided. Access door orientation is not indicated on the plan.
applicableAreas: All transformer pad access door sides

findings.comment: Transformer pads are shown but access door orientation is not indicated on any pad. No dimension callouts document 10-foot clearance from access door side. Spatial analysis suggests some pads may be constrained by building proximity.
applicableAreas: All five transformer pad locations on Sheet 21

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not provide cross-sections or detail drawings showing whether any transformer pad is located in a niche, vault, or enclosed area on three or more sides (confined space configuration). Without cross-section drawings demonstrating either 35-foot vertical clearance (if niche) or confirmation that the location is not confined space, the 15-foot versus 10-foot clearance requirement cannot be determined.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if in confined space)

findings.comment: Overhead electric line (OHE) is shown on landscape plan but specific 15-foot radius clearance measurements from transformer locations to overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors (measured from conductors, not pole centerline) are not dimensioned.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution conductor locations

findings.comment: Overhead distribution facilities are referenced on the electrical plan as 'Overhead Electric' but are not detailed showing conductor routing, pole locations, heights, or clearance envelopes. No documentation exists showing whether buildings, parking garages, light poles, signs, billboards, chimneys, antennas, or tanks are installed under or over Austin Energy overhead distribution facilities. Without detailed overhead line routing and clearance documentation, this prohibition cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads and proposed site structures/equipment (if overhead distribution facilities present)

findings.comment: Overhead distribution line locations are shown on the landscape plan (OHE symbol). No customer facilities (buildings, parking garages, light poles, signs, structures) are clearly identified as being positioned directly under or over overhead distribution lines based on the site plan layout.
applicableAreas: Overhead distribution line areas

findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fencing (identified by H.6 key notes for wooden privacy fences) but provides no clearance dimension callouts from the fence faces to outside conductor of overhead electric lines. No dimension annotations demonstrate the 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Provide dimension callouts on site plan and fence detail sheets showing clearance from outside conductor to fence face and posts.
applicableAreas: Privacy fences and site perimeter fencing shown on landscape plan near overhead electric conductors

findings.comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility pole locations. Landscape plan (Sheet 31) shows fence alignments. However, no dimension callouts document the horizontal distance from fence posts to existing electric poles. Plans must show that fence posts are located minimum 10 feet from pole centerlines. Provide dimension annotations on site/landscape plan showing distance from each fence post location to nearest utility pole.
applicableAreas: Fence post locations on site where existing utility poles are present

findings.comment: Transmission notes on Sheet 3, Block 9 indicate transmission facilities exist on or adjacent to site, but no clear transmission line routing map is provided showing easement boundaries relative to proposed fencing. Without voltage confirmation and transmission easement delineation, cannot determine whether fences are beneath/within transmission easement and therefore subject to non-conductive material and grounding requirements. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on site plan, confirm fence specifications (non-conductive material and grounding details) if within easement.
applicableAreas: Fencing shown in proximity to electric transmission lines if transmission easement applies

findings.comment: Site plan shows parking areas and driveways, and grading plan shows finished surface elevations, but no section views document vertical clearance from parking pad surface to overhead electric lines. Plans must include section views with dimension callouts showing clearance from parking pad elevation to lowest overhead conductor point (16 feet for parking without truck traffic, 18 feet with truck traffic, 12 feet minimum for residential pedestrian areas). Additionally, a note on plans must identify the clearance requirement. Provide section views with vertical clearance dimensions and a plan note documenting required clearance.
applicableAreas: Vehicle parking and display areas on concrete pads beneath overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 indicates transmission facilities are present and notes restrictions for areas within 25 feet of transmission structures. Grading plan shows driveway and road surface elevations but provides no section views documenting 30-foot minimum vertical clearance from road/driveway surface to electric transmission lines. Verify transmission line locations, provide transmission easement boundary on plans, and provide section views showing road/driveway elevation with vertical clearance dimension to transmission lines (minimum 30 feet).
applicableAreas: Roads and driveways beneath transmission lines

findings.comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles along Valley View Road frontage. Site plan shows sidewalk alignments along the property boundary. However, no dimension callouts or notes verify that sidewalks are cleared from existing power poles at each end of the property along right-of-way. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from sidewalk edges to pole locations at north and south property limits, or provide relocation/adjustment notes if poles are in conflict.
applicableAreas: Sidewalks at property ends along right-of-way frontage near existing power poles

findings.comment: For a 39-unit multi-family project, trash receptacles or enclosures are expected but their specific locations are not clearly documented on site plan in relationship to overhead electric lines. If trash bins are located beneath overhead conductors, raised trash bins during service collection must maintain minimum 7.5-foot sky-to-ground clearance from the outer conductor. Identify trash collection locations on site plan with dimension callouts showing clearance from OHE, or provide notes confirming trash areas are outside the clearance zone.
applicableAreas: Trash enclosure and receptacle locations on site

findings.comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows electrical meter locations but does not document water meter locations relative to overhead electric service-drop conductors. Water meters must maintain minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from outside conductor of service drops. Provide utility plan with water meter locations dimensioned from overhead service-drop routing, or confirm water meters are located clear of service drop conductor zone.
applicableAreas: Water meter locations relative to overhead electric service drops

findings.comment: Site plan shows building footprints and property lines. Existing and proposed electric facilities require clearance space in areas adjacent to property. Permanent foundations within 5 feet of property line may not allow necessary clearance space for electric utility facilities and their future maintenance access. Provide dimension annotations on site plan showing distance from building foundation edges to property line, particularly where electric poles or facilities are located adjacent to property boundary, or confirm that adequate clearance space is maintained for utility access.
applicableAreas: Permanent building foundations located within 5 feet of property line

findings.comment: Landscape plan shows outdoor lighting fixtures but does not document clearances from these fixtures to overhead electric conductors. Both 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance and 15-foot radial clearance must be verified. Site plan notes state decorative lighting must be full cut-off and fully shielded per Land Development Code, but clearance from overhead lines is not addressed. Provide dimension callouts on landscape plan showing clearance from light fixture locations to outside conductor, or provide relocation notes for fixtures within clearance zones.
applicableAreas: Decorative outdoor lighting fixture locations near overhead electric lines

findings.comment: Sheet 3, Block 9 (Electric Transmission Notes) indicates transmission structures are present on or adjacent to site. Transmission structures often require angled down guy wires extending to ground anchors. Easement exhibit must show dedicated easement for transmission down guy anchors extending 10 feet either side of guy wire alignment plus minimum 50 feet beyond end of anchor point. Verify transmission structure down guy anchor locations and provide transmission guy anchor easement dimensions on plat/easement exhibit.
applicableAreas: Down guy anchor locations for transmission structure support cables

findings.comment: For residential service-mast through-roof installations with voltages ≤300V, clearance requirements differ: 3-foot minimum above roof, or 18-inch minimum if mast is within 4 feet of roof edge. No building elevation sheets showing service-mast through-roof installations have been provided in the site plan package. If service masts are proposed through roofs, building elevation sheets must document mast locations and roof clearance dimensions. If service masts are not used (all underground service), this requirement is not applicable. Clarify service installation method and provide elevation documentation if roof-mounted masts are proposed.
applicableAreas: Service-mast through-roof installations on proposed buildings

findings.comment: Bicycle parking racks are shown on detail sheet 22 (Construction Details 1) with spacing requirements, but no cross-reference is made to transformer pad locations on the electrical plan. Without transformer pads identified on the construction details or with dimensions marked from bike racks to transformer pads, the 5-foot minimum clearance cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if bike racks adjacent)

findings.comment: Gas service infrastructure and pressure specifications are not clearly shown on the electrical or utility plans reviewed. Specific gas line locations relative to transformer pads cannot be evaluated.
applicableAreas: Gas line locations near transformer pads

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not indicate whether any transformer pad is located in a niche (accessible from outside but within building footprint), enclosed area, or notched-out building configuration. No cross-section drawings demonstrating vertical clearances within niche access paths are provided. Without this documentation, the applicability and compliance status of the 35-foot vertical clearance requirement cannot be determined.
applicableAreas: All transformer pads (if in niche configuration)

findings.comment: The electrical plan does not identify any niche service installations. No architectural specifications showing 3-hour fire wall ratings are provided in the plan set. No electrical plan notes document consultation with Austin Energy Design business unit regarding niche configurations. Without documentation of niche service proposal and its associated requirements, this item cannot be evaluated.

findings.comment: Transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan (Sheet 21) but are NOT depicted on the plat (Sheet 2). Because transformer pad locations are not shown on the plat in relation to property lines, easements, or public right-of-way, it is impossible to verify that all five pads are 100% on private property and not in public right-of-way or straddling property lines.
